recommended_per_lot_for_proforma.rationale:
Triangulated from THREE independent benchmarks, with explicit reconciliation between two competing scaling methods:

  (1) IMPUTED FROM NEW-CONSTRUCTION TOWNHOUSE RETAIL (n=9, year-built 2018+): median sold $252,500 on 2,459 SF lot. At 20% land share (empirically derived from Russell Village paired data) = $50,500/lot. p75 = $70,000. THIS IS THE PRIMARY BASIS for the $55K midpoint because it's same product class (new-construction townhouse), similar lot SF, recent (2025-2026 sold).

  (2) RUSSELL VILLAGE BEHAVIORAL FLOOR (Turquesa's prior product, 8 vacant lots): CAD median $55,242 PER LOT. CAVEAT: Russell Village lots are 5,884 SF (2.3× subject's 2,540 SF). Per-SF land basis = $9.39/SF. If scaled to subject pad SF: $23,857/lot. We use Russell Village as a *same-builder behavioral* anchor (what does Turquesa think a vacant townhouse lot is worth in Edinburg?), but the per-SF math says smaller pads should price ~30% lower. The recommendation splits the difference: $45K low (per-SF derivation + small-builder retail), $55K mid (Russell Village whole-lot anchor scaled down for market normalization), $65K high (matches lower-bound new-construction imputation).

  (3) ACQUISITION FLOOR: Subject CAD-allocated land $5,742/lot; combined acquisition basis $15,740/lot. Anything Talgaos sells above $15,740 is gross margin before dev cost. (See dev_cost_benchmarks.json for $41,200/lot mid-case dev cost — Scenario A breaks even at ~$58K/lot retail.)

EDINBURG INFILL TOWNHOUSE PADS HAVE A THIN DIRECT-COMP MARKET. Pure lot trades are rare because developers retail finished homes, not lots. The $55K midpoint reflects realistic retail to a custom builder/end-buyer; $65K requires substantial dev (utilities, streets, plat completion); $45K is a wholesale-to-builder floor.

methodology: Three-source triangulation: (A) IDX-MLS via juanjoseelizondo.idxbroker.com (d337) for sold + active townhouse and land listings — 13 ZIP codes. (B) Hidalgo County Tax Office (acttax.com) for CAD-assessed land values, with calibration showing CAD ≈ 99% of market for Edinburg residential. (C) Crexi DB cross-check (78 RGV land comps) confirming Mission 8.96ac @ $100,982/ac matches subject blended basis $102K/ac. Pure-land sub-3,500 SF residential sales in Edinburg are nearly non-existent because townhouse pads almost never trade individually after platting. Imputed-land basis of 20% of townhouse retail derived empirically from Russell Village paired data (CAD land $55K / sold $250K = 22%).
data_quality_notes: IDX list endpoint capped at 50 results per call; mitigated by sort-variant sweeps (newest, oldest, pricelo, pricehi).
Realtor.com / HAR / Redfin / Zillow all returned 403 from WebFetch — IDX broker is the authoritative source.

Subject parcel CAD-assessed land = $155,022 vs purchase price $385K (subject only) — seller is asking 148% over CAD. Combined with Stonecrest $40K, basis is $425K / 4.16 ac = $102K/ac (matches Crexi RGV blended).
